source.title: Minimal, Local, Causal Explanations for Jailbreak Success in Large Language Models

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper refines global accounts of refusal by testing local, token-specific causal patches made along SAE concept vectors. Its own results show that several local changes can recover refusal on successful jailbreaks, but do not directly compare the single difference-in-means direction against alternative representational geometries.
record.gate_note: The paper tests local SAE-feature patching on successful jailbreak prompts, not the original difference-in-means direction. It reports causal refusal recovery and numbers of patches, which bear on V4's multi-component/refinement question. Baseline methods are compared, but their plot values are not extracted here because they are not interventions on the claim's single direction. The paper also discusses harmfulness and refusal being separate, but those are claims attributed to cited work, not results of this study.
record.test_reason: The study does not test any version. It never computes, ablates or adds the difference-in-means refusal direction, and it does not measure how jailbreaks change projections onto it. Its results are its own method's (LOCA) performance at restoring a first-token refusal on successful jailbreaks, by patching SAE concept vectors with activations from the refused original prompt, compared against two baseline methods. Patching to a reference activation along many SAE features says nothing about whether refusal is one direction, a cone or affine (V4). The claim that 'global' accounts like Arditi et al. are too coarse is a motivating argument backed by citations, not by a test of the direction. The case study interprets SAE concepts, not the refusal direction. The reader's T5/V4 'supports' label is therefore unfounded.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that LOCA gives minimal, local, causal explanations of jailbreak success. It needs about six interpretable patches on Llama, where prior SAE methods routinely fail within 20. Instruction tokens matter in early layers and post-instruction or punctuation tokens in later layers. They name the first-token refusal proxy and SAE interpretability as the main limitations.
record.recipe_differences: Instead of finding a harmful-minus-harmless mean-activation direction and projecting it out or adding it across layers and positions, LOCA iteratively patches selected token activations along SAE decoder concept vectors using matched activations from a refused original prompt. The procedure is local to each jailbreak example and token.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported patch counts and successful layers vary across models: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct uses 6-8 patches on early layers; Gemma-3-27B-IT reaches success from layer 36 onwards with an average of 9; Gemma-2-2B-IT generally induces refusal by layer 10 with an average of 12; Qwen-38B by layer 22 with an average of 10. The localization analysis also reports different token selections by layer.

fits_no_version.finding: Few token-specific SAE-concept patches, taken from the refused original prompt, restore first-token refusal on successful jailbreaks. This takes about 6-8 patches on Llama-3.1-8B, 9 on Gemma-3-27B, 12 on Gemma-2-2B and 10 on Qwen. Selected tokens shift from instruction tokens in early layers to post-instruction and punctuation tokens in middle layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak success can be explained locally by a small, sample-specific set of SAE-feature changes, with causally important token positions varying by layer.

record.problems: The main refusal rate and several optimization metrics use only the first output token, and the authors describe failure cases for that proxy. Full-response HarmBench evaluation is limited to a random subset of 50 Llama samples. The eligible jailbreak samples are filtered by model and are not balanced across attack types; the Gemma-3 text also reports 438 eligible samples while saying a set of 140 was evaluated. The study does not test preservation of benign capabilities or compare its local patches directly against the single difference-in-means direction. Authors note that earlier-layer SAE interpretations were time-intensive and error-prone.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows omitted from the extracted text-described results. Layer-by-layer curve values and comparator-method values in Figures 3, 8, and 11 were not transcribed because the figures provide plotted values without readable numeric data in the text.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is extracted, ablated or added, and no capability check is made.
No measure of whether jailbreaks suppress the refusal direction. The argument that jailbreaks use sample-specific mechanisms rests on citations and SAE interpretation, not on the direction.
No comparison of single-direction versus cone, affine or multi-direction accounts. Multi-feature SAE patching toward reference activations does not test this geometry.
Discussed only via cited work (Zhao et al. 2025a, Zou et al. 2023a).

record.verdict_notes: This is a method/interpretability paper. Its only links to the refusal direction are a baseline (Lee et al. 2025), which uses Arditi's direction as a target, and a comparison of patch counts with Arditi's all-token steering. Neither is a test of a version. The rows are all own-method performance and should be unlinked.

versions.untested_parts: Does not find or ablate the harmful-minus-harmless difference-in-means direction, add it, or test preservation of general abilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Does not test whether attacks suppress the single direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.

Tests local causal patches along multiple SAE concept vectors, not whether refusal geometry is specifically affine, conic, or a dominant direction plus others; no direct comparison with a single-direction account across ordinary refusal prompts.
The separation of harmfulness and refusal is discussed only through cited prior work; this study does not measure the two separately.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or other transfer test of the refusal direction.
No comparison of refusal-training methods, timing, or training stages.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Iteratively patched jailbreak-prompt residual embeddings along SAE concept vectors using matched activations from the refused original prompt.

conditions.value: early layers; specific layer not stated for the 6-8 average

rows.measure: Patching operations needed to induce refusal
rows.value: On average, 6-8 patching operations on early-layer residual embeddings
rows.note: The paper reports an average range, not a per-sample distribution.
rows.check: Own-method performance (patches needed by LOCA), not a measure of refusal-direction geometry. Abstract gives an average of six. Baseline is the prior methods, which mostly fail within 20 patches, not 'not stated'.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Iteratively patched jailbreak-prompt residual embeddings along SAE concept vectors using matched activations from the refused original prompt.
rows.measure: Refusal rate, defined in the main evaluation by matching the first output token to the original prompt's first output token
rows.note: The paper states that LOCA reaches 100% at layer 7; Appendix F separately evaluates full responses on a random subset.
rows.check: Own-method refusal rate (first-token match) after SAE patching. It does not bear on V4 or on any version.

rows.subject: Gemma-3-27B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Iteratively patched jailbreak-prompt residual embeddings along SAE concept vectors using matched activations from the refused original prompt.

conditions.value: 438 eligible; the paper says a set of 140 was evaluated

rows.measure: Patching operations associated with successful refusal recovery
rows.value: Success reached in intermediate layers (layer 36 onwards) with an average of 9 patching operations
rows.note: The paper reports the average and layer range in prose; it does not give per-layer numeric values there.
rows.check: Own-method performance. Only 140 of 438 eligible Gemma-3 samples were evaluated. The text's '100% at layers 7 and 38' attributes 38 to Gemma-2, which is likely a Gemma-3 typo.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-2B-IT
rows.operation_detail: Iteratively patched jailbreak-prompt residual embeddings along SAE concept vectors using matched activations from the refused original prompt.
rows.measure: Patching operations generally needed to induce refusal
rows.value: Refusal is generally induced by layer 10, requiring an average of 12 patches
rows.note: Appendix C gives this result in prose.
rows.check: Own-method performance on Gemma-2-2B-IT. Not a test of any version.

rows.subject: Qwen-38B
rows.operation_detail: Iteratively patched jailbreak-prompt residual embeddings along SAE concept vectors using matched activations from the refused original prompt.
rows.measure: Patching operations associated with successful refusal recovery
rows.value: Refusal is successfully induced by layer 22, requiring an average of 10 patches
rows.note: The paper reports the layer and average in prose.
rows.check: Subject is misread. The paper's 'Qwen-38B' cites the Qwen3 technical report, so it is likely Qwen3-8B (8B, not 38B). Own-method performance only.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Applied two local SAE-concept activation patches to a successful AutoDAN jailbreak prompt about illegally acquiring firearms, replacing selected jailbreak activations with matched activations from the refused original prompt.
rows.value: Refusal induced after two activation patches
rows.note: The first patch increased concept #31126 strength by 1.50; the second decreased concept #125009 strength by -1.48, after which refusal was induced.
rows.check: Single-example case study of SAE-concept patches (layer 11). It does not involve the refusal direction.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: Applied five local SAE-concept activation patches to the same successful AutoDAN jailbreak prompt, replacing selected jailbreak activations with matched activations from the refused original prompt.
rows.value: Refusal induced after five activation patches
rows.note: The authors say most selected patches concentrated on punctuation tokens; the final patch increased a concept associated with generally harmless questions, which they note may be misinterpreted.
rows.check: Single-example case study (layer 3). The authors admit the final concept is likely misinterpreted. No bearing on any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: LOCA local SAE-feature patching on eligible successful jailbreak pairs, across the reported chat models and the AutoDAN case study
reader_labels.reason: Refusal was recovered through iterative patches along multiple local concept vectors, including the two- and five-patch case-study sequences (r1, r3-r7); this supports a local multi-change refinement, though it does not establish a specific geometric model.
